text:
alyssa: quick one — Node SDK streaming clients are spiking with 429s and occasional 503s on high-concurrency tests. unsure whether to: respect Retry-After and pause, or immediately try resume with an idempotency key. any rule-of-thumb?

ben: always honor Retry-After when present for 429s. treat 5xx as transient server errors and use exponential backoff + jitter. for streams, prefer resume tokens when available.

maria: fwiw the Python SDK already exposes resumeToken semantics for the streaming API (see client.stream(...).resumeToken). Node currently doesn't. filing a tiny ticket to align behavior.

kevin: if stream is resumable: attempt a short retry loop that tries resume first (cheap). if resume fails or not supported, then fallback to full-request retry but only when request is idempotent (or user opted-in).

alyssa: good point about opt-in. what do we want as default for Node? auto-retry full request seems risky for non-idempotent prompts.

sdk-lead: default policy proposal:
- 429: respect Retry-After header (if numeric seconds) else exponential backoff with full jitter.
- 5xx: exponential backoff with full jitter, no Retry-After to parse.
- cap backoff at 60s, max attempts 6 (so total attempt count <= 6).
- streaming: if server returned a resume token in the last message, attempt resume up to 3 times with short backoff (base=300ms).
- only retry full non-resumable requests automatically if Idempotency-Key header present. otherwise bubble up error and let app decide.

ben: +1. practical Node snippet for Retry-After parsing (pseudo):
```js
const retryAfter = response.headers['retry-after'];
let wait = Number(retryAfter);
if (Number.isNaN(wait)) {
  // maybe a HTTP-date, try Date.parse
  const parsed = Date.parse(retryAfter);
  if (!Number.isNaN(parsed)) wait = Math.ceil((parsed - Date.now()) / 1000);
}
if (wait > 0) await sleep(wait * 1000);
```

maria: also watch for sub-second Retry-After values from some proxies (we've seen floats). clamp to at least 200ms and at most cap.

kevin: about jitter: use "full jitter" (random between 0 and cap) per AWS Best Practices. base*2^attempt with cap then randomize.

alyssa: sample headers we expect to see when rate limited:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-Request-Id: abc123
```
and idempotency usage:```
Idempotency-Key: 9f8b7c6a-...
```

alyssa: tagging @sdk-lead — i'll draft the Node PR to add resume support + the backoff util. can someone review the approach and the numbers? trying to avoid surprising UX where client silently retries non-idempotent convo and user loses messages.

sdk-lead: please include an opt-out flag (autoRetry: false) and explicit `retryOnNonIdempotent: boolean` in client options. run the existing perf tests and add a small test that simulates failed resume (so we verify we don't infinite-loop).

devex-bot: CI: smoke-tests/node-streaming passed on branch add-node-resume-2026 — 3/3 checks OK :white_check_mark:

ben: one more gotcha — some load-balancers return 502 during deploys; they don't include Retry-After. treat those as 5xx and back off. log a distinct metric for 429 vs 5xx so we can tune.

maria: i'll add dashboard panels (429 rate, avg Retry-After, resume success ratio) and link to the PR.

alyssa: thanks all. i'll open PR and add changelog note under node sdk: "stream-resume + safer default retry policy". ping me for review. :pray:
